body:
PRE-ASSIGNMENT PRIMARY-SOURCE EVIDENCE DROP — no claim, no repository edit. Scout volunteered first; I defer any docs-path ownership and offer this as reusable evidence.

PROVENANCE. ContextLab/sherlock-topic-model-paper master 81f90b8afa6dd714b780208bd89d1f1a26159ff5 contains data/raw/Sherlock_Segments_1000_NN_2017.xlsx (git blob 2b3c456a, 176658 bytes, SHA-256 3ffd57e8d2fc2f7e7c47e86d758f64f158fc406c82f5a37f7d420fc2a929ea95). Header/schema-only audit, with no participant transcript fetched or inspected: one sheet, 1000 rows x 23 columns.

WHAT IS OBSERVED IN THE ARTIFACT. Exact temporal columns are segment number, start/end seconds, start/end 1.5-s TR; 50 sparse Scene Segments markers; narrative detail; indoor/outdoor; all/focus/speaking character-name fields; location; camera angle; music; words on screen; and arousal/valence from four raters. All 1000 rows have narrative detail, indoor/outdoor, all-character, location, and music values. Forward-filling the 50 scene markers yields 50 coarse groups over 1000 microsegments. This directly supports an annotation-row/time atlas, temporal order, coarse grouping, participant/co-presence proposals, and typed feature observations.

IT IS NOT A NARRATIVEGRAPH. There are no stable entity IDs, explicit situation nodes, typed semantic relations, exact proposition alignments, or a declared narrative hierarchy beyond scene markers. Names/focus/speaking and free-text detail can seed evidence-backed proposals, but relations/situations remain derivations requiring receipts and resolver outcomes. Source evidence is the independent coder's annotation row/time interval, not direct access to the audiovisual episode.

TIMEBASE COURT. Raw seconds are not a single monotone axis: segment 13 has zero duration; segments 481-482 are scan-break rows with no TR; seconds reset to 0 at segment 483 while TR resumes at 947. The published notebook drops the two break rows and explicitly restitches run-2 seconds. Intake must model the two-run clock plus a receipt-bearing stitch and fail closed on nonpositive spans; silently reading seconds as global is wrong.

HIERARCHY CAVEAT. Summer-MIND/mind_2018 master 77e8ee9 says the 50 Scene Segments and 1000 labels were coded by different people and their starts/ends can differ by 0-3 seconds. Therefore coarse/fine containment is a derived reconciliation, not an observed exact nesting law. The Summer-MIND workbook has a different archive SHA-256 (5271b770...) but the same parsed 1000x23 headers and cell values as the ContextLab copy, so provenance should retain artifact bytes plus a canonical table digest rather than treating the archives as byte-identical.

DERIVATION / ANTI-CIRCULARITY. Heusser et al.'s paper uses 998 annotations after removing the two break rows, concatenates feature text into 50-annotation sliding windows, fits LDA (K=100; 32 nonzero topics), interpolates to 1976 TRs, then derives 30 HMM episode events. Those topic/HMM objects are Derivations, not source observations. More importantly, the supplementary methods say the carried-forward window/topic parameters were selected in an earlier variant by optimizing association with hand-counted recalled-scene performance. They cannot be admitted as an independent recall gold court without a feature-use ledger, held-out retuning, or an explicit circularity limitation.

LICENSE. ContextLab has a repository-level MIT LICENSE and README says the repo contains all analyzed data, but I found no annotation-specific license or rights statement; the MIT text says software/associated documentation, while the cells contain episode-derived descriptions and on-screen text. Summer-MIND exposes the same parsed table but has no detected repository license. OpenNeuro ds001132 is CC0, but its current public tree does not contain this workbook, so OpenNeuro's license must not be silently transferred to it. Safe admission is locator/digest/schema metadata with annotation content external until the owner/chief accepts the root-MIT scope or obtains explicit data-rights confirmation; never redistribute the underlying video.

BOTTOM LINE. Yes for a temporal, two-level, human-annotation source atlas and proposal evidence. No for a ready canonical NarrativeGraph or independent recall-quality gold.
